claims.quote: Vienoto valsts interneta plūsmu apmaiņas punktu izveido un uztur, lai: 1) pastāvīgi nodrošinātu kritiskās datu plūsmas atrašanos tikai Latvijas Republikas teritorijā

claims.title: Nacionālās kiberdrošības likums (National Cybersecurity Law), Art. 32

claims.quote: akreditēta informācijas sistēma – Satversmes aizsardzības biroja noteiktā kārtībā reģistrēta un akreditēta informācijas sistēma, kurā apstrādā klasificēto informāciju
claims.quote_english: accredited information system: an information system registered and accredited in accordance with the procedure set by the Constitution Protection Bureau, in which classified information is processed
claims.title: MK noteikumi Nr. 822 (19.12.2023) Valsts noslēpuma, NATO, ES un ārvalstu institūciju klasificētās informācijas aizsardzības noteikumi, para. 2.1

indicators.research_note: Judged partial. The general rule for state and municipal bodies was Cabinet Regulation No. 442 (2015), para. 5.1. It required data to be stored in a NATO, EU or EEA member state. That regulation lapsed on 18.10.2024 (https://likumi.lv/ta/id/275671). Its successor, Cabinet Regulation No. 397 (2025) on minimum cybersecurity requirements (https://likumi.lv/ta/id/361481), has no general storage-location clause for government data that I could find. It restricts outsourcing for critical-infrastructure A-class systems by nationality and registration (NATO/EU/EFTA/IP4, para. 94). It also limits auditors to processing data in NATO/EU/EFTA territory. The National Cybersecurity Law Art. 30 delegates data-centre placement rules to the Cabinet, with a deadline of 01.04.2025. No such regulation appears among the acts issued under the law. The binding location rules that remain are sector-specific: critical data flows must stay in Latvian territory (Art. 32), and classified information may only be processed in systems accredited by the Constitution Protection Bureau (SAB).

review.reason: Art. 32 of the National Cybersecurity Law does require critical data flows to stay only in Latvian territory, which is a sector-specific rule; the Reg. 822 quote is only a definition and ties classified processing to SAB-accredited systems, so 'partial' holds but not 'yes'.

claims.quote: Informāciju, kas ir valsts noslēpums, pēc svarīguma klasificē sevišķi slepenā, slepenā un konfidenciālā informācijā un informācijā dienesta vajadzībām.
claims.quote_english: Information that is a state secret is classified by importance as top secret, secret and confidential information, and information for official use.
claims.title: Likums "Par valsts noslēpumu" (Law on State Secrets), Art. 3(1)

indicators.research_note: Classification levels are defined in statute: the Law on State Secrets, Art. 3. Detailed protection rules are in Cabinet Regulation No. 822 (2023).

review.reason: Art. 3(1) of the Law on State Secrets, verified verbatim, defines the classification levels (top secret, secret, confidential, official use) in statute.

indicators.research_note: I checked the National Cybersecurity Law (likumi.lv/ta/id/353390), Cabinet Regulation No. 397 (2025), the acts issued under the Cybersecurity Law (likumi.lv related-acts listing), and the LVRTC cloud project pages. None of them has a cloud certification scheme requiring immunity from non-EU law. Regulation No. 397 has only audit requirements for cloud and data-centre providers, based on NIS2. I found no authoritative statement that no such scheme exists, so the value is unknown rather than no.

review.reason: No claims were cited and no source confirms or denies a sovereign cloud certification, so 'unknown' is the correct value.
